#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script> -- <TASK_ID>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=t-emf-l
#   --output=log_train_emf_lhc_%a.log
#   --nodes=1
#   --cpus-per-task=4
#   --mem=32GB
#   --time=7-00:00:00
#   (gpu request commented out)

#flux: --job-name=t-emf-l
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 4
#flux: --time-limit=168h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=32GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --output=log_train_emf_lhc_%a.log
# Slurm's %a token (array index) is not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose a unique filename.

# NOTE: The script uses $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID but no Slurm array directive was provided.
# Under Flux, accept the task id as the first argument.
TASK_ID=${1:-0}

source activate ml
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

cd /scratch/jb6504/manifold-flow/experiments

python -u train.py -c configs/train_mf_lhc_june.config --algorithm emf -i "$TASK_ID"

reasons: The original Slurm job requested 32GB of memory (`--mem=32GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
